name: GLUE
description: General Language Understanding Evaluation is a collection of 9 English NLU tasks covering linguistic acceptability (CoLA), sentiment (SST-2), paraphrase detection (MRPC, QQP), semantic similarity (STS-B), and textual entailment (MNLI, QNLI, RTE, WNLI). It also includes a hand-crafted diagnostic suite for linguistic phenomena. The benchmark was foundational in the BERT era.
evaluation_method: accuracy, F1, Matthews correlation, Pearson/Spearman correlation (task-specific)
general_score_metric: composite score (average of scaled task scores)
typical_sota_score: 90%+ (saturated; BERT-era models broke the human baseline; fully obsolete for frontier models)
reputation: Foundational benchmark of the transformer era; cited in thousands of papers; historically central to NLU evaluation from 2018–2021; now considered obsolete for frontier models
notes: Saturated within one year of BERT's release. Leaderboard is now frozen. Criticised for annotation artifacts in some tasks (e.g., WNLI) and a lack of discourse-level or complex reasoning tasks. Superseded by SuperGLUE and then by MMLU for knowledge evaluation. No longer used for any frontier evaluation.
